value.body: A science degree in computing: programming, data structures, databases, operating systems, networks and discrete mathematics, often alongside Mathematics or another science subject. It is more theory- and maths-oriented than a BCA and shorter than a B.Tech CSE. It leads to software and data jobs, an MCA or M.Sc, or further study.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in the science stream, usually with Mathematics (many colleges require it for Computer Science). Central universities (Delhi University, BHU and others) admit through CUET-UG scores in the relevant subjects; many state universities and their colleges admit on Class 12 merit or a state test. You usually choose the major — or a combination of two or three subjects — at admission.

value.title: At a glance
items: Software employers often hire B.Sc graduates, but some campus drives and job listings ask for B.E./B.Tech only.
Common next steps: an MCA (NIMCET for NITs, state tests, CUET-PG), an M.Sc, or a job.
Projects, internships and coding practice matter as much as the degree for tech hiring.
Government routes are mostly general-graduate exams (SSC, banking, state PSCs).
